tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis:
The recorded session logs into Magento Admin, navigates to the Manage Products grid, closes the notification popup via a stable clickable element, fills out all available product filters (ID range, Name, SKU, Type, Attribute Set, Price range with currency, Qty range, Visibility, Status, Website), executes Search, uses Reset Filter, clears and re-applies filters, and inspects pagination and grid results. The previous failure was due to waiting for a non-existent selector a[title="close"]. The new recording demonstrates that the notification popup can reliably be closed by clicking the specific element with element_hash df76c6ce85 (indexes 102/119 depending on overlay) and that all grid filters correspond to specific inputs/selects with stable indices and hashes.

2) Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, given a set of Magento product grid filter parameters (ID range, Name, SKU, Type, Attribute Set, Price range, Qty range, Visibility, Status, Website), navigates to the Manage Products grid, closes the notification popup if present, applies the filters using the grid filter row, runs the Search, and returns the resulting grid contents. The tool must avoid using brittle selectors like a[title='close'] and instead rely on stable element hashes for deterministic interaction.

3) Action Plan:
- Navigate directly to the Magento Admin catalog product grid URL.
- (If login form appears) Log in via the known username/password fields.
- Close the global notification popup via its stable clickable element.
- Populate each filter control (ID from/to, Name, SKU, Type, Attribute Set, Price from/to, Qty from/to, Visibility, Status, Website) only when an input value is provided.
- Click the Search button to apply filters and wait briefly for grid reload.
- Extract the visible grid data (column headers, rows, pagination info) as structured content.

Because this tool is single-purpose (search/filter + results), we will NOT implement Reset Filter, pagination navigation, checkbox selection, or Edit link clicking as part of the core tool; they were demonstrated in the run but are not essential to the main goal of performing a filtered product search.

4) Variable Identification:
All variable inputs correspond to actual grid filter fields or options observed in the recording:
- entity_id_from / entity_id_to: numeric ID range under ID column.
- name: text under Name column.
- type: product type select (visible texts: "Simple Product", "Grouped Product", etc.).
- attribute_set: attribute set select (visible texts: "Default", "Electronics", etc.).
- sku: text under SKU column.
- price_from / price_to: numeric price range (USD) under Price column.
- qty_from / qty_to: numeric quantity range under Qty column.
- visibility: select ("Not Visible Individually", "Catalog", "Search", "Catalog, Search").
- status: select ("Enabled", "Disabled").
- website: select (e.g., "Main Website").
Additionally, since login may be required at the start URL, we keep credentials parameterized (even though they are fixed in this environment) for completeness: admin_username, admin_password.

5) Step Optimization:
- Use a single navigation step to the catalog_product URL instead of multi-click menu navigation.
- Use deterministic interactions via elementHash for all inputs/selects/buttons, based on the recording:
  - Login: username (3597a5c5e6), password (1c47a5217e), login button (6831836d17).
  - Popup close: df76c6ce85.
  - Filters: 6c749b372d (ID from), c43947da3b (ID to), 29fed4031b (Name), 59a067e4b4 (Type select), 97d647bb6f (Attribute Set select), f127a4b0da (SKU), 8e38c5e838 (Price from), 927c2c13e5 (Price to), 0a91de9a0e (Qty from), bdecbf7d2c (Qty to), fef9e4ddbc (Visibility select), 2d0526510b (Status select). Website select has index 161 in screenshots but no element_hash captured; it is rarely needed and defaults to Main Website, so we treat it as optional and omit deterministic interaction to avoid brittle selectors.
- Replace previous fragile waiting for selector a[title='close'] with a direct click on element_hash df76c6ce85, and add a small wait after login and after Search.
- Do not implement Reset Filter, pagination navigation, or checkbox/Edit interactions, as they are not strictly necessary for the core search/filter task.

Given Magento's grid implementation, filter application is done via POST, so URL parameter optimization is not appropriate; we keep UI form interactions.

Because element presence/timing for login and popup can vary, we will:
- Always navigate to the grid URL.
- Attempt login fields via deterministic element hashes; if page is already logged in, those elements will not exist but the navigation will still land on the grid. In this tool definition we cannot express conditionals, so the consumer should start from a logged-in state whenever possible. In typical use per instructions, the agent is already logged in, so login-related steps can be skipped in execution or ignored if elements are missing.

Overall, the tool will:
1) Navigate to catalog_product grid.
2) Close popup (element_hash df76c6ce85).
3) Fill filter fields based on provided parameters.
4) Click Search (element_hash 90708cd5ce / 5ff1fd4054 / ddb931c1ad types, but consistently the Search button in header with element_hash 90708cd5ce from first interaction).
5) Wait for reload.
6) Extract resulting grid data.

The input schema below reflects only the filter parameters and credentials; all are optional except credentials if login is needed, but per problem statement we can assume authenticated session so they are marked optional.
name: tool_search_products_v3
description: Search and filter products in the Magento Admin Manage Products grid using multiple filter controls, then return the resulting product grid data.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin Manage Products grid URL.
Wait for the Manage Products grid or potential login page to load.
Input admin username on the login form if visible. This will be a no-op if already logged in.
Input admin password on the login form if visible.
Click the Login button to submit the admin login form, if present.
Wait for redirect from login to the Manage Products grid.
Close the Incoming Message notification popup using its stable element, avoiding unreliable generic selectors.
Set ID From filter value if provided; otherwise input will be empty and ignored by Magento.
Set ID To filter value if provided.
Set Name filter text if provided.
Select Product Type filter option if provided.
Select Attribute Set Name filter option if provided.
Set SKU filter text if provided.
Set Price From filter value (USD) if provided.
Set Price To filter value (USD) if provided.
Set Qty From filter value if provided.
Set Qty To filter value if provided.
Select Visibility filter option if provided.
Select Status filter option if provided.
Click the Search button to apply all specified filters to the product grid.
Wait for the product grid to reload with filtered results.
Capture the filtered product grid content for downstream processing or validation.
steps.goal: Extract the Manage Products grid data after filters have been applied, including pagination info, column headers, and all visible rows with their Edit URLs.

input_schema.name: admin_username
input_schema.description: Magento admin username to use on the login form if it appears (e.g., 'admin').

input_schema.name: admin_password
input_schema.description: Magento admin password to use on the login form if it appears (e.g., 'password123').

input_schema.name: entity_id_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for product ID filter (From). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: entity_id_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for product ID filter (To). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: type
input_schema.description: Product Type filter select visible text.

input_schema.name: attribute_set
input_schema.description: Attribute Set Name filter select visible text.

input_schema.name: price_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound for Price filter (From, in USD).

input_schema.name: price_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound for Price filter (To, in USD).

input_schema.name: website
input_schema.description: Website filter select visible text (typically 'Main Website').
